title: Samsung and Google Smart Glasses Launch at a $395 Base Price
summary: Samsung and Google launch smart glasses at a 395 dollar base price
detailed: Samsung and Google have unveiled their intelligent eyewear, blending accessibility, navigation, and daily convenience into a lightweight design.

Powered by Google’s Gemini assistant and running on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon AR1 Gen1 platform, the glasses offer features like real-time translation in over 70 languages and turn-by-turn navigation via Google Maps.

sentences: Samsung and Google have unveiled their intelligent eyewear, blending accessibility, navigation, and daily convenience into a lightweight design.

Powered by Google’s Gemini assistant and running on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon AR1 Gen1 platform, the glasses offer features like real-time translation in over 70 languages and turn-by-turn navigation via Google Maps.
With prices starting at $395 and frame options from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, they cater to both functionality and style, as highlighted by TechAvid.

Explore how these glasses integrate with devices like Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel, and iPhone, and gain insight into their 9-hour battery life and privacy safeguards, including face redaction and LED recording indicators.
You’ll also discover how Gemini enhances accessibility with guided vision and object recognition.
This exposé breaks down the hardware, software, and practical use cases, offering a comprehensive look at what to expect when shipments begin in December.
Samsung and Google have launched their intelligent eyewear, now available for pre-order.
Designed to assist with accessibility, navigation, and daily tasks, the glasses feature Google’s Gemini assistant and are compatible with select Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel, and Apple iPhone models.
Pre-orders are managed by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, with shipping scheduled for December.
The eyewear collections cater to various style preferences, with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster offering distinct designs.
Both brands provide options for prescription lenses, sunglasses, and photochromic lenses to suit different needs.

The glasses run on Qualcomm’s Snapdragon AR1 Gen1 platform, with 2 GB of RAM and 64 GB of storage.
A 12-megapixel camera supports 3K video recording at 30 frames per second with image stabilization.
Audio is delivered through two open-ear speakers, supported by four microphones.
Connectivity includes Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.4.
Weighing approximately 40 to 41 grams, the glasses are designed for all-day comfort.
While they lack a built-in display, their functionality is extensive.
Battery life is rated at up to 9 hours per charge, with the charging case providing over seven additional charges, totaling up to 72 hours.
The case, weighing 194.5 grams, can recharge the glasses to 60% in about 30 minutes.
Google Gemini powers the glasses, using the Android XR platform to provide contextual assistance.
Users can activate Gemini with a wake phrase or touch controls to ask questions about their surroundings.
The assistant can identify landmarks, explain menu items, and recognize objects via the camera, all without needing a phone.
The glasses support real-time translation in over 70 languages through Google Translate, making them useful for multilingual communication.
Integration with Google Maps offers spoken turn-by-turn navigation, while Google Meet allows users to share their perspective during video calls.
Additional features include music playback, podcasts, audiobooks, and notifications from a connected phone.
Accessibility features include guided vision, which provides conversational descriptions of surroundings to assist blind and low vision users.
The glasses also connect with IRA, a service linking users to human visual interpreters via the camera.
Privacy measures include automatic face redaction before images are processed by Gemini, microphone systems that prioritize the wearer’s voice, and permissions for camera and microphone access.
An LED indicator shows when visual data is being saved.
Google has stated that captured data will not be used for advertising or Gemini training.
Third-party apps are restricted from enabling real-time facial recognition or bypassing recording indicators.
Demonstrations showcased Gemini’s ability to extract event details from a concert poster, add them to Google Calendar, and assist with travel planning.
However, some reviewers noted challenges when switching between conversations with Gemini and nearby individuals.
Repeating Gemini’s responses occasionally caused the assistant to re-engage unnecessarily, leading to an overwhelming audio experience.
Gentle Monster began pre-orders on November 12th, with shipping starting December 9th and the official launch on December 10th.
Warby Parker expects initial deliveries by mid-December.
While the glasses are part of Google’s Android XR ecosystem, they do not require an Android phone to operate.
The Samsung and Google intelligent eyewear offers practical applications, particularly in accessibility and navigation.
The hardware and features show promise, but the software’s ability to handle real-world scenarios will be crucial.
With a starting price of $395 and compatibility across major platforms, the glasses may attract users seeking a balance of functionality and style.
However, as the host concludes, the ultimate test will be whether Gemini’s performance and the glasses’ battery life meet expectations in everyday use.
